clue.text: Enormous appeal in reserve, endlessly agreeable

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second
without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
'it' is sex appeal, as in an 'It girl'
nice means pleasant or agreeable

explanation.surface: Someone with huge charm who keeps it in check is endlessly pleasant company.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer force; 'endlessly' trims only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic is an adjective for something of colossal size, after the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Preacher using one stage, central point raised in middle of screen?

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so the run reads backwards
placed in the middle of a word, this goes inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the navel is the centre point of the body, or of anything
to screen for a disease is to test for it

explanation.surface: A preacher performing on one stage, raised high in the centre of the TV screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen suggests television, which fits the answer, but here it means to test, as in screening for a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A televangelist is a preacher who broadcasts sermons on television.

clue.text: More palatable time since row

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Food tastes better now that the argument is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier is the comparative of tasty, meaning more pleasant to eat.

clue.text: Cent man put after nickel in slot

indicators.note: put after places these pieces following the next one in the answer

blocks.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
c is the abbreviation for cent
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man feeding coins, a cent and a nickel, into a vending machine slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nickel and cent are both American coins in the surface; nickel is the chemical element here.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or a fitting position, a slot where something belongs.

clue.text: Test resistance in ice club cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged
in here adds this letter to the words that follow before they are rearranged

blocks.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strength trial at an ice-hockey club, where the ice finally cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: Test looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a severe trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a severe trial or testing ordeal, from the vessel in which metals are heated.

clue.text: Go over weakness

blocks.note: first meaning: to desert to the other side, as a spy or soldier might
second meaning: a flaw or shortcoming

explanation.surface: It reads as advice to revise a weak point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' suggests reviewing something; here it means switching allegiance. The verb and noun are spelt alike but stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to desert to a rival cause; as a noun it means a flaw.

clue.text: Dismal drain to receive attention

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it inside

blocks.note: to drain something is to dry it out
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A gloomy drain finally getting some maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and gloomy, the same as dismal.

clue.text: Dandy harbouring passion about item of military kit

indicators.note: harbouring something means sheltering it inside

blocks.note: a fop is a man vain about his clothes
rage is a violent passion
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A dandy with a passion for some piece of army gear.
explanation.walkthrough: About is not an indicator but a piece: ca is the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A forage cap is a soldier's peaked cap worn off duty, so it is part of military uniform.

clue.text: Burn invention, being a fool

blocks.note: to char is to scorch
a lie is an invented story

explanation.surface: Someone who torches their own invention is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: A Charlie is British slang for a fool, as in 'a right Charlie'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British colloquial use a charlie is a silly person, so the word stands for a fool.

clue.text: Hopeless campaign turns back into contemptible type

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start
putting one thing into another places it inside that word

blocks.note: turns on a variety bill are acts
a louse is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A doomed political campaign reverses course and ends up in the hands of a nasty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like a verb but is the noun for performances; reversed, it sits inside LOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an undertaking with no chance of success, an apt phrase for a hopeless campaign.

clue.text: Referring to composer not having British hit

indicators.note: not having something means that letter is left out

blocks.note: re means concerning or with reference to
Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
B is a standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A note about a composer who never had a hit in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus BACH without its B gives REACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a target is to hit or get to it, as when a shot reaches its mark.

clue.text: Odd hush near an unsettled country game

indicators.note: unsettled letters have been shaken up out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange silence falls before a nation's sporting fixture is decided.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; unsettled does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare and hounds is a cross-country chase in which runners follow a trail laid by the hares.

clue.text: Mean to carry over fine material

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: vile means mean or wretched
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone intends to carry some delicate fabric across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean to' reads as 'intend to', but Mean is an adjective here, and O goes inside VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a thin, semi-transparent cotton or silk fabric used for curtains and dresses.

clue.text: Urge strangely admitted by silly liar, right out of order

indicators.note: done strangely, the letters come out in an odd order
silly suggests jumbled, so these letters are rearranged too
something admitted by another is let in, so it goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd impulse is owned up to by a foolish fibber, which is quite improper.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams are at work: one indicator for each set of letters, with one set nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular describes something against the rules or not in proper sequence, as is anything out of order.

clue.text: Drama with race gripping millions as a rule

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama
a rally is a motor race
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A thriller about a race with big money at stake, the usual formula.
explanation.walkthrough: Japanese No (or Noh) drama is a crossword favourite for these two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually or ordinarily, the same sense as the phrase as a rule.

clue.text: Pride in treatment of organ with care

indicators.note: a treatment of material processes it, reshaping its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon takes pride in handling a donated organ carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing sense of one's own importance, the bad sense of pride.

clue.text: Eye's covering odd pieces from so-called artist

indicators.note: odd pieces are the letters in the first, third, fifth and seventh places

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and seven of the word
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A self-styled artist's work offers bits that only cover the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called artist' looks like one sneering phrase; it splits into a letter source and an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The sclera is the tough white outer layer covering most of the eyeball.

clue.text: Angry minister interrupted by call for attention

indicators.note: a word interrupted by another has it break into its middle

blocks.note: a cleric is a minister of religion
ho is a cry to attract attention

explanation.surface: A cross vicar whose sermon was cut short by a shout from the pews.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric means hot-tempered or irritable, from the old humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: Spot occupied by bishop behind head of ecumenical board

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
a place occupied by someone has them inside it
behind says this part comes after the other in the answer

blocks.note: the opening letter
a spot or blemish is a mark
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A seat taken by a bishop at the back of a church council meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee to sit on; it is the verb, as in boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go on board a ship or aircraft, the verb sense of board.

clue.text: Drop in support for music

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to hang is to drop or dangle

explanation.surface: Funding for music has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhangra is a lively style of popular music rooted in Punjabi folk dance.

clue.text: Measure of acidity in stark conclusion of field marshal

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
the conclusion of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: sheer means utter or stark, as in sheer folly
pH is the chemist's scale of acidity
the final letter

explanation.surface: A chemistry test result sitting starkly in a field marshal's final report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field marshal' reads as a military rank; the phrase splits, and marshal alone is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to guide or herd them along, which is to marshal them.

clue.text: Cut up, supply question

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means written upwards, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: to axe is to cut
a mine is a rich supply or source, as a mine of information

explanation.surface: Being upset and wanting to give a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut up suggests distressed; the two words split, cut a piece and up its reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine a witness or candidate is to question them closely.

clue.text: Stand and fight, first off, with captain's heart

indicators.note: with its first letter taken off, the word is shortened at the front
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: to strive is to struggle or fight
the central letter of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to hold your ground and battle, led by the captain's courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand and fight' reads as one order; Stand alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand or metal support for a pot or kettle.

clue.text: Maiden and I worry about uranium beside river

indicators.note: going about something surrounds it, so that letter goes inside
beside places the next part alongside, at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
to nag is to worry or pester
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
the Ural, a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: A young woman and I fret over a nuclear fuel by a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden looks like a girl in the scene, but it is the adjective, as in a maiden speech or voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural speech or voyage is the first of its kind, the same sense as maiden.

clue.text: Philosopher's note in instruction at bottom of page?

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: PTO, please turn over, printed at the foot of a page
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A thinker's memo tucked into the footnote of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the philosopher has LA inside PTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates and author of the Republic.

clue.text: Tidy pair with naughty child

blocks.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: Two parents clearing up after a mischievous youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to smarten or tidy one's appearance fussily.

clue.text: Try wearing metal cross

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so this word goes within the next

blocks.note: tin is a metallic element
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Advice to put on a metal crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like a crucifix, or anger; it is a noun for a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a cross between two species.

clue.text: Red paint put around to stop pests

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read backwards
to stop a gap something goes inside it, plugging the middle

blocks.note: oil is oil paint
vermin are pests such as rats and mice

explanation.surface: Red paint daubed about as a deterrent to pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red paint' reads as one phrase; the definition is Red alone, and paint is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a brilliant scarlet red, originally a pigment made from cinnabar.

clue.text: Express disappointment about weak religious books

blocks.note: a lame excuse is a weak one
NT, the New Testament

explanation.surface: Grumbling over feeble holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: About belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: one laments something, not about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to mourn or voice regret over it, a transitive verb like the definition.

clue.text: Evergreen comedy lacking interior force

indicators.note: without its inside, only the outermost letters of the word survive

blocks.note: the first and last letters
to press is to force or push

explanation.surface: A long-running comedy that has lost its inner energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Evergreen suggests a show that never dates; here it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a conifer that keeps its dark foliage all year, so it is an evergreen tree.
